coverage_register_defect: DECISION_COVERAGE.json (schema_id pm.packet_decision_coverage.v1, packet "usage") asserts exactly six fields per topic: id, title, requirement (prose), packets (the list of topic packets that carry the decision - all 107 include "usage"; runtime 84, chat 68, settings 60, prompt 43, onboarding 29), category, and status. status is the literal string "fixed" on all 107 topics with zero exceptions, zero "open"/"partial" values, and no per-topic history. What it therefore ASSERTS: that the packet author considers each decision adjudicated and settled in this cumulative packet, and which sibling packets must carry it. What it does NOT assert, and cannot be read as asserting: any evidence field, artifact path, file, DOM selector, field name, enum value, fixture id, test id, screenshot, commit, verification date, verifier, owner, or acceptance criterion; any statement that a Usage concept (QwenUsageConcept or any other) implements or demonstrates the decision; any distinction between "the packet states the decision" and "an artifact satisfies the decision"; any severity, priority, or hard-failure marking; and any per-surface scope (the packets field is a routing hint, not a claim that a Usage surface exists for the topic - e.g. PRM-010 DAP DebugSession and PROC-001/002 prompt structure list "usage" yet have no Usage-reportable surface). Consequence for audit: status:"fixed" is packet-side adjudication state, not coverage or implementation evidence; it can neither pass nor fail a concept, and it supplies no machine-checkable key - which is why this file exists. A conformance run must therefore treat every topic as UNVERIFIED until the search_keys below are resolved against concrete concept artifacts.
